decision_lens: The test for legibility/metis is whether a proposal creates a distinct STATE-SIMPLIFICATION axis (how much a country's governance apparatus has traded local adaptive capacity for administrative visibility) with its own resistance/backlash coupling, versus merely restating existing state_capacity or surveillance (internal_security) as if legibility were already captured — the specific Scott claim is that HIGH legibility can itself be destabilizing (destroyed metis reduces a population's shock-absorption capacity), which is a different causal shape than 'more state capacity is better,' so a proposal that only makes state_capacity a bigger lever is not modeling Scott. The test for Girard is whether a proposal creates an actual escalation-through-imitation dynamic (conflict intensity that grows from agents/countries copying rivals' postures rather than from independent grievance accumulation) and a scapegoat-discharge valve (a mechanism by which accumulated tension is dumped onto a designated target, reducing diffuse pressure at the cost of concentrated harm to the target) — a proposal that just adds another SocialUnrest source is not Girard; the mimetic and discharge structure is the whole content of the theory. The test for civil-war onset is whether Fearon/Laitin FEASIBILITY (terrain/state-reach/financing) is represented as a condition SEPARATE from grievance/pressure intensity — the central empirical finding is that high-grievance, low-feasibility countries do NOT have civil wars and low-grievance, high-feasibility countries sometimes do, so any mechanism that only scales existing pressure levels cannot reproduce the feasibility-gates-onset finding; check specifically whether internal_security's existing fields (police_capacity, surveillance, terrorism_risk, restraint) already encode a state-reach/feasibility proxy or whether genuinely new state is needed, and whether Collier-Hoeffler's financing-sustainability dimension has any plausible host at all (diplomacy sanctions? shock rosters? or nothing).
focus: Whether the simulation can express James Scott's legibility/metis dynamics (state simplification projects that render populations administratively visible at the cost of destroying local practical knowledge, and the backlash/resistance that illegible practices generate), René Girard's mimetic-rivalry and scapegoating mechanism (desire and conflict that escalate through imitation rather than material scarcity, resolved — or not — through a unifying sacrificial/scapegoat mechanism), and the quantitative civil-war-onset literature (Fearon & Laitin's insurgency-feasibility model, Kalyvas's micro-level violence-logic, Collier & Hoeffler's greed-vs-grievance framing) as mechanisms hosted at or coupled through internal_security, as opposed to being fully absorbed into the existing undifferentiated SocialUnrest/PoliticalInstability pressure pair
name: fd-legibility-mimesis-civilwar-onset
persona: Apply the perspective of a comparative-politics and political-anthropology scholar working three traditions together: James C. Scott (Seeing Like a State) on legibility — state projects (cadastral surveys, standardized IDs, monoculture administration) that trade situated practical knowledge (metis) for administrative visibility, often destroying the very local adaptive capacity that made a system resilient; René Girard (Violence and the Sacred) on mimetic desire — conflict escalating not from scarcity but from rivals imitating each other's desires, with scapegoating as society's mechanism for discharging accumulated mimetic violence onto a substitute victim; and the empirical civil-war-onset literature — Fearon & Laitin's finding that insurgency FEASIBILITY (rough terrain, weak state reach, financeable rebellion) predicts onset better than grievance intensity, Kalyvas's argument that violence during civil war follows local, not just national, logics of control and denunciation, and Collier & Hoeffler's greed-vs-grievance framing of what makes conflict financially sustainable once started.
review_areas: Whether a legibility/metis proposal creates a distinct state-simplification stock coupled to a resistance/backlash pathway (rather than reusing state_capacity or surveillance as a stand-in), and whether it correctly identifies that Scott's claim is destabilizing in the HIGH-legibility direction, not just the low-capacity direction that InternalSecurity/Governance already cover

Whether a Girard mimetic-rivalry proposal actually implements imitation-driven escalation (one country's/agent's posture shift propagating to rivals via a copying mechanism, not just via the existing NEIGHBOR_MAP cascade's capacity-mediated propagation) and a scapegoating discharge valve distinguishable from ordinary pressure decay — check whether Diplomacy's bilateral relations (sentiment, ideology_distance) or the shock roster's 'elite power struggle' event type are plausible low-cost hosts for either half

Whether the civil-war-onset mechanism represents feasibility (terrain/reach/financing) as a gating condition independent of grievance/pressure level, hosted at internal_security per the objective's mandate — specifically checking police_capacity, surveillance, terrorism_risk, and restraint (§9) for which, if any, already function as a feasibility proxy versus requiring new state, and whether Collier-Hoeffler's financing-sustainability leg has any plausible host or should be flagged as unhostable in the current lattice

Whether Kalyvas's micro/local-logic argument (violence patterns differing by local control contestation, not just national pressure level) is realistically in scope given the simulation has no sub-country spatial resolution — and if out of scope, whether the proposal correctly scopes down to what IS representable (a country-level onset/intensity mechanism) rather than overclaiming a Kalyvas-faithful implementation

Whether any of the three mechanisms collides with existing internal_security fields or the certified Phase-2 elite-ratio EliteFracture discharge pathway, and whether 'modulate, don't inject' is honored — i.e. do these mechanisms gate/scale existing InternalSecurity→Legitimacy/Unrest/EliteFracture couplings rather than adding parallel always-on pressure sources

Whether cost estimates for all three mechanisms are placed on the S/M tier ladder against the Phase-1/Phase-2 actuals with an explicit reason tied to how much new accumulator state each requires versus how much is pure coupling modulation

severity_examples.condition: Directly contradicts Fearon & Laitin's central empirical finding (feasibility, not grievance, predicts onset) — a grievance-only mechanism reproduces the theory the literature explicitly refuted, and would need to be flagged as a misattribution even if it were otherwise well-built
severity_examples.scenario: A civil-war-onset mechanism is proposed that scales InternalSecurity's existing pressure emission by a grievance-intensity multiplier alone (higher unrest/instability = higher onset probability), with no feasibility gate of any kind

severity_examples.condition: This is not Scott's thesis at all — it is the conventional state-capacity-is-good framing Scott is explicitly arguing against; a faithful mechanism must be capable of producing INCREASED instability from a legibility push, not just decreased instability from more capacity
severity_examples.scenario: A legibility mechanism is framed as 'more state_capacity reduces unrest' with no backlash/resistance term for the metis-destruction side of Scott's argument

severity_examples.condition: Loses the sacrificial-victim structure that is Girard's entire point — a scapegoat mechanism must impose a cost on a designated target as the other side of the relief ledger, or it is just an unexplained pressure sink, which also risks re-triggering the 'no conservation/redistribution bookkeeping anywhere' gap named in §2 of the inventory rather than closing it
severity_examples.scenario: A Girard scapegoating valve is proposed as a straightforward relief mechanism (discharges SocialUnrest to zero for a target country) with no accounting for concentrated harm delivered TO the scapegoat target

severity_examples.condition: Misses the cheapest available host (an existing, already-live cross-country channel) in favor of new parallel machinery, inflating calibration cost against the B7 discipline
severity_examples.scenario: The mimetic-rivalry escalation mechanism is proposed as new state duplicating NEIGHBOR_MAP's existing capacity-mediated cascade math without checking whether imitation-driven escalation could instead be a coupling-strength modulator on the existing 10-country hardcoded map

success_hints: Reward proposals that correctly identify feasibility (terrain/reach/financing) as CAUSALLY SEPARATE from grievance/pressure intensity and represent it as a distinct gating condition rather than another multiplier on existing pressure

Reward a legibility mechanism whose backlash term can produce a country where HIGH state_capacity/legibility coexists with RISING instability — the specific non-monotonic signature that distinguishes Scott's thesis from ordinary capacity-is-stabilizing framing
Reward a Girard mechanism that explicitly closes or explicitly acknowledges the conservation-bookkeeping gap (inventory §2, affordance #6) rather than silently adding another unpaired sink

Reward explicit scoping-down of Kalyvas's micro-local claims to what is representable at country-level resolution, with the gap between theory and representable state stated plainly rather than glossed over
Penalize any of the three mechanisms proposed as a new always-on additive pressure family rather than a coupling modulator on internal_security's existing outputs
